title: Plain lecture, 25–30 minutes
_note: Forked 2026-09-07 from plain-lecture v1, which is IMMUTABLE (linearity and vector-spaces bind it). The only change is the target length and the rule that comes with it. Bindings are byte-identical to v1 so a module moved here re-renders nothing.

writer.doc: videos/linearity/script.md (header) — the register was written in the script itself
writer.sentence: Say the thing, show the thing, move on.
writer.register: Short declaratives. No em-dash chains. No 'not X, it is Y'. Second person, present tense. Every formula carried by the prose around it.
writer.acts: A cold open that asks the everyday question; parts that each answer one thing; a closing that says what the next part stands on.
writer.length_rule: 25–30 minutes is the target, not a wall — a little over or under is fine when the content asks for it. Material that would run an hour is SPLIT into modules, never compressed into one; the split is a registry decision (two slugs), not a script decision. At ~150 wpm (speed 1.15) that is roughly 3,000–4,350 words of narration. Education is the point; entertainment is the window into it.
writer.cold_open: Five short beats, one animation resolving through them, no bed.
writer.music_policy: none by default; a module may author a bed

bindings._note: Only keys a shot list block may carry belong here: they land in beats/ fragments byte for byte. Prose about policy goes under `writer`.
